rows.en:
EX-Gear Basics: Supply Transport
These explanations assume the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Title line names the drill (basic EX-Gear controls: supply transport). EX-Gear modes rendered Walk / Hover / Flight mode.

rows.en:
Lock on to a container and move close
to it, and you can
pick it up.

Press the □ button to set
the container down where you are.

You can only carry containers
in Walk mode or Hover mode.

Also, be careful: you can't
attack while you're
carrying a container.

Lock on to a door switch and move close
to it, and you can
operate the switch.

Hold Down on the D-pad while locking on
to lock on to containers and
switches first.

Now practice transporting supplies.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Switching Modes
These explanations assume the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

You can switch the EX-Gear's mode
with the analog stick.

Push the analog stick down for Walk mode,
left or right for Hover mode,
and up for Flight mode.

In every mode, you can move
your unit with the D-pad.

In Walk mode, press Up, Down, Left or Right
on the D-pad to move that way.
rows.notes: Japanese: Up/Down/Left/Right move forward/back/left/right; compressed to 'move that way' for width.

rows.en:
Now go ahead and begin your
mode-switching training.

Leaving this room
ends the training.
Sample obtained.

Force enemy surrender
(destroy only their mechs)
rows.notes: Mission objective: make enemy soldiers surrender (destroy only their machines). TM line was too wide; reworded.

rows.en: Let's go over the basics of Fighter mode.

During training, flight mode is set to
Normal Flight, and controller settings are
reset to defaults. Please keep this in mind.

Press Up on the D-pad to nose down and
descend, and Down to nose up and climb.
Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.

Hold the L button and press Left or Right
on the D-pad to yaw.
(Real Flight only)

Press the × button to boost.
You can keep boosting until the
boost gauge is full.

Quickly press Down on the D-pad twice
to fire reverse thrust and decelerate sharply.

Hold the △ button to
brake and slow down.

Push the analog stick up
to transform into Fighter mode.

That covers the basics of Fighter mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any mode other than Fighter.

Now go ahead and begin your
Fighter mode flight training.

Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
Let's go over the basics of Battroid mode.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

Press Up, Down, Left or Right on the D-pad
to move forward, back, left or right.

At the end of a step, keep holding
the D-pad to dash.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost downward
and lose altitude.

Push the analog stick down
to transform into Battroid mode.

That covers the basics of Battroid mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any mode other than Battroid.

Now go ahead and begin your
Battroid mode training.
Let's go over the basics of GERWALK mode.
Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.

In GERWALK mode, you hold your altitude
and hover.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost downward
and lose altitude.

Push the analog stick left or right
to transform into GERWALK mode.

That covers the basics of GERWALK mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any other mode.
rows.notes: TM ended 'into any mode other than GERWALK'; shortened to 'any other mode' for the short third line.

rows.en:
Now go ahead and begin your
GERWALK mode training.
Let's go over shooting attack basics.

Hold Down on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to containers
or switches.

While locked on, hold the L button
and quickly tap the R button
to release the lock-on.

Press the □ button to attack the locked-on
enemy with your main weapon.

Press the ○ button to attack the locked-on
enemy with your special weapon.

If your unit has several special weapons,
hold the L button and press the □ button
to switch between them.

Some special weapons are capable of
multi-lock-on, which locks on to
several enemies at once.

To multi-lock-on, hold the ○ button
to lock on to multiple enemies
within range.

Release the ○ button during multi-lock-on
to hit every enemy locked at that moment
with your special weapon.

While the locked-on enemy is ahead of you,
your lock-on level goes up.

Shooting with a raised lock-on level
gives you bonuses to attack power
and accuracy.

These shooting controls are the same
in Fighter, Battroid
and GERWALK modes.
That covers shooting attack basics.
Let's go over melee attack basics.

In GERWALK and Battroid modes,
press the △ button to make a melee attack.

The number of hits in a combo varies
by unit and mode.

The higher your pilot's melee stat,
the more hits your combos get.

Hold the △ button for a moment, then
release it to perform a
charged melee attack.

Press the △ button while dashing
to perform a dash melee attack.

In Battroid mode, chain melee attacks
while holding Down on the D-pad
to perform a launching melee attack.

A launched enemy is left defenseless
for a short time.
You can attack it further during that time.

In Battroid mode, press the △ button
to hit a downed enemy with a down attack.

Please note that Fighter mode
has no melee attacks.
That covers melee attack basics.
Now I'll explain Special Maneuvers 1.

In Fighter mode, while locked on,
hold the R button to turn
and bring the enemy dead ahead.

In Battroid mode, hold the L button
to guard.
Guarding reduces the damage you take.

Guarding while no enemy is locked on
resets the camera angle
to face forward.

While guarding, press Up, Left or Right
on the D-pad to move
without dropping your guard.

In GERWALK mode, hold the L button
to hover and hold
your position.

While hovering, press Left or Right on the
D-pad to strafe while facing forward.

You can also step left or right and dash
while strafing.

In Battroid or GERWALK mode, press the
× button right after taking a knockdown hit
to avoid getting knocked down.

And even if you do get knocked down,
mashing the × button lets you recover
from being down faster.

If you have a wingman, press the SELECT
button together with the D-pad
to issue tactical commands.
